newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WEEK AHEAD-Australia market watches share surge.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD-Australia market watches share surge.

text.p: All eyes will be on the Australian stock market this week after its record run over the past month, while interest elsewhere is likely to be dampened by a lack of local data.
ECONOMICS

The week again remains barren of major local data meaning that main game for markets will be trying to second guess monetary authorities both here and in the U.S. who will hold policy setting meetings next week.
Local markets remain confident, or in the case of the dollar resigned, that there will be another rate cut. The question is one of timing.
The Reserve Bank of Australia board meets on July 1, but can change rates at time. If the RBA favours an easing, it is expected to wait on the outcome of the U.S. FOMC meeting on July 1 and 2.
A U.S. rate hike would not rule out a local cut, but may affect its timing, analysts said

If the FOMC raises U.S rates on July 2, which the market no longer expects, analysts said the RBA may wait until after inflation and wages data in July before cutting rates, to give markets time to adjust to local rates falling below U.S. rates.
Only two pieces of data are due this week.
Job vacancies and overtime figures for the May quarter are scheduled for release on Thursday and new motor vehicle registrations data for May are due out on Friday.

The job vacancies data will be more closely watched, though it is hard to forecast. The stagnant labour market has been seen as influential in the four rate cuts to date, and signs of a downturn would bolster the confidence of interest rate bulls.
A strong number may meet a mixed reaction because recent forward labour market indicators have suggested stronger growth than has actually occurred.
Registrations data is normally overlooked by the market, but a dearth of data and the weakness in April retail trade and June consumer confidence, will see more attention paid than usually.

Registrations rose 10 percent in the first quarter, but dropped six percent in April. Another weak number would add to perceptions that the strong start to consumer spending in 1997 was a blip and that underlying demand remains subdued.

AUSTRALIAN BONDS (Fri: 10 yr cash yield 7.06 pct, 3-yr 5.87) The bond market faces another week of very little local data, and only a smattering of U.S. indicators, suggesting that trading interest will remain fairly slim.

However, the approach of the Reserve Bank board meeting on July 1 and the possibility that this will be followed by a further cut in official interest rates is likely to see the market end the week on a firm note, traders said.

Recent U.S. indicators have also suggested that the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1 and 2 may refrain from tightening policy, but local speculation is that the RBA will want to see confirmation of this before easing policy.
The recent spate of weak Australian data, apart from the housing sector, has seen a 50 basis point cut in 5.5 percent official rates more or less priced in to the September bill futures contract.

Ten-year bond yields touched their lowest level in 3-1/4 years at the beginning of last week and fell through 7.0 percent, although there has subsequently been something of a correction with the market lacking the momentum to carry the rally on in the absence of key data.
AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR (Fri: US$0.7511/16, New York US$0.7500/10)
Te Australian dollar remains constrained by speculation of a further cut in official interest rates after July 1.
The 90-day bank bill contract for September, a good guide to market thinking on rates, was at 94.86 on Friday, implying a rate of 5.14 percent compared to the present official rate of 5.50 percent.
At the same the market is factoring in a possible interest rate rise in the U.S. from the present 5.50 percent Fed Funds rate, which would put further pressure on the Australian dollar.
Domestic data due out this week is seen as having little impact on the local currency.
AUSTRALIAN STOCKS (Fri: All Ordinaries, 2,712.6 up 2.2 pct)
Australian shares are expected to maintain their record levels after a wave of confidence from overseas investors in the resource and banking sectors carried local stocks to a record close on Friday.
The All Ordinaries Index ended at 2,712.6, up 57.3 points or 2.2 percent for the week, after reaching an all-time high of 2,714.2 during Friday's trading.

"While this market continues to be strengthened by international markets and domestic thoughts that official interest rates may be lowered again, there's really no thought that the trend will take a reversal," said Jamie Spiteri of Shaw Stockbroking

The benchmark All Ordinaries index set its sixth closing high in seven days on Friday, while Wall Street also maintained its positive tone, setting another record to finish up 19 points on Friday at 7797.
Traders said banks were among the star local performers as investors chased yield, and resources were also strong.
BHP, which is due to release its full year results on Friday, pushed through the A$20 mark before easing to end up 13 cents at A$19.85.
Share analysts have revised up their profit forecasts for Australia's biggest listed company after it announced a strong rise in copper production.

The revisions put the steel-making and resources giant on track for a slightly higher annual net profit of between A$1.35 billion and A$1.4 billion before abnormal items for the year ended May 31, 1997.
